title: How tall is the toy's shadow, with the torch near and far?
description: A toy stands in front of a wall and a torch shines on it. The board shows the rays from the torch making a small triangle to the toy and a big triangle to the wall, then scales the toy's height to find the shadow with the torch near and with the torch far. Keeko's doubt is that the shadow is as tall as the toy.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rays spread from the torch, so the shadow is the toy's height times torch to wall, divided by torch to toy. Watch for students who think the shadow is as tall as the toy.

video_script.why: The child scales the toy's height by the ratio of two distances, because spreading rays make a small and a big triangle of the same shape.
video_script.substitution: Shadow = toy height x (torch to wall) / (torch to toy).
video_script.anchor: a torch, a toy and a wall in a line, seen from the side, with two rays from the torch past the top and bottom of the toy
video_script.wrong_answer: the shadow is as tall as the toy
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the shadow is as tall as the toy. The rays spread out from the torch, so at the wall they are wider apart than the toy.
video_script.payoff_line: The shadow is twenty centimetres near, and about thirteen point three centimetres far

final_answer.spoken: twenty centimetres, then about thirteen point three centimetres

never_show: a shadow of 10 cm marked as right
maths_rules: toy height 10 cm; toy to wall 50 cm; torch to toy 50 cm
torch to wall = 50 + 50 = 100 cm, twice the torch to toy distance
torch moved: torch to toy 150 cm; torch to wall = 150 + 50 = 200 cm
the farther the torch, the closer the shadow is to the toy's own height, 10 cm, which is the projection
slip: the shadow is as tall as the toy, 10 cm
video_script.design: One side view: torch, toy and wall on a line, two rays spreading from the torch. The distances and the shadow are labelled; the torch slides back in the third step.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a toy 10 cm tall stands 50 cm in front of a wall; a torch shines at the wall from 50 cm in front of the toy

marks.toy: the toy appears in front of the wall with its height and its distance from the wall
marks.torch: the torch appears in front of the toy with its distance marked
marks.ask: an empty box appears on the wall, then the torch slides back to 150 cm with another empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a shadow on a wall.
<bookmark mark='toy'/>A toy is ten centimetres tall and stands fifty centimetres in front of the wall.
<bookmark mark='torch'/>A torch shines straight at the wall from fifty centimetres in front of the toy.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How tall is the shadow? What if the torch moves back to one hundred and fifty centimetres?

beats.on_screen: the toy, the torch and the two empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: side view: two rays from the torch pass the top and the bottom of the toy and spread to the wall; a small triangle to the toy and a big triangle to the wall are shaded; a second drawing with the rays side by side

marks.rays: two rays leave the torch and spread, passing the top and bottom of the toy
marks.tri: the small triangle to the toy and the big triangle to the wall are shaded
marks.same: the two triangles are laid over each other to show the same shape
marks.proj: a second drawing shows the rays side by side and the outline on the wall glows

narration: <bookmark mark='rays'/>Rays of light leave the torch and spread out as they travel to the wall.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>The rays make a small triangle to the toy and a big triangle to the wall.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Both triangles start at the torch and have the same shape.
<bookmark mark='proj'/>Rays that run side by side to the wall make an outline called the projection.

beats.on_screen: Given: toy height 10 cm; toy to wall 50 cm; torch to toy 50 cm, then 150 cm

marks.given: the four given distances are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the toy is ten centimetres tall and stands fifty centimetres from the wall.
The torch is fifty centimetres from the toy, and then one hundred and fifty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the height of the shadow, torch near and torch far

marks.find: the words height of the shadow are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the height of the shadow for both places of the torch.

beats.on_screen: Torch to wall = torch to toy + toy to wall = 50 + 50 = 100 cm

marks.add: the two distances are written and added

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, find the distance from the torch to the wall.
Add torch to toy and toy to wall. Fifty plus fifty is one hundred centimetres.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>That is twice the distance from the torch to the toy.

beats.on_screen: shadow = toy height x torch to wall / torch to toy = 10 x 100 / 50 = 20 cm

marks.calc: 10 x 100 / 50 = 20 cm is written in the shadow box

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, scale the toy, because the two triangles have the same shape.
The shadow equals the toy height times torch to wall, divided by torch to toy.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Ten times one hundred, divided by fifty, gives twenty centimetres.

beats.on_screen: the torch slides back to 150 cm; torch to wall = 150 + 50 = 200 cm

marks.back: the torch slides back to 150 cm
marks.add: 150 + 50 = 200 cm is written for torch to wall

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, move the torch back to one hundred and fifty centimetres.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add one hundred and fifty and fifty. Torch to wall is now two hundred centimetres.

beats.on_screen: shadow = 10 x 200 / 150 = about 13.3 cm; the toy's own height 10 cm is a dashed line on the wall

marks.calc: 10 x 200 / 150 = about 13.3 cm is written in the second shadow box
marks.dash: a dashed line for the toy's own height appears on the wall beside the shadow

narration: <bookmark mark='calc'/>Step four, scale the toy again. Ten times two hundred, divided by one hundred and fifty, is about thirteen point three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='dash'/>The dashed line shows the height of the toy itself.

marks.trend: the second shadow glows beside the dashed line

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The shadow is twenty centimetres near, and about thirteen point three centimetres far.
Both shadows are taller than the toy.
<bookmark mark='trend'/>The farther the torch, the closer the shadow is to the projection of the toy.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the drawing
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows a shadow drawn as tall as the toy; the rays are shown still spreading and the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows a shadow drawn as tall as the toy
marks.spread: the two rays are shown spreading past the toy
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the taller shadow glows

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the shadow is as tall as the toy.
<bookmark mark='spread'/>But the rays keep spreading out from the torch, all the way to the wall.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>At the wall they are wider apart than the toy, so the shadow is taller than the toy.
